Gnosis Interpretation
MOVE tracks Treasury volatility and term-premium stress: below 80 is calm, 80-120 is moderate uncertainty, and 150+ is high stress; 110.45 is moderate. SOFR is secured overnight funding (3.88% effective Sep 29), not a stand-alone stress verdict. NFCI measures broad financial conditions; its -0.55 reading indicates looser conditions. The 10Y yield at 5.29% is up 3 bp on the latest Treasury session.

Fed & Policy Watch
  • Today has four Board speaker events (Waller 10:00 AM, Jefferson 1:30 PM, Bowman 3:00 PM, Cook 3:30 PM ET); Cook is moderated by New York Fed President Williams. Speeches/discussion can reprice rates, but are not FOMC decisions.
  • FOMC minutes from Sep 15-16 publish Oct 7 at 2:00 PM ET. The next scheduled FOMC decision is Oct 28; none falls in this briefing window.
  • New York Fed Treasury operations for Sep 15-Oct 14 plan about $15.6B in reinvestment purchases and no reserve-management purchases; routine liquidity backdrop, not a one-time injection.
  • Policy headline watch: the White House U.S.-China Board of Trade (Sep 27) identifies product lists for possible reciprocal reduced-tariff treatment, subject to domestic law and process. No implementation date is specified; treat any change as headline risk, not a timed catalyst.
Omissions and Watch
  • BLS direct schedule request returned HTTP 403. Official BLS release-specific and October 2026 schedules were readable through the official web fallback: Employment Situation is Oct 2 at 8:30 AM ET. CPI (Oct 14) and PPI (Oct 15) are outside Oct 1-8; no CPI or PPI is included in this window.
  • The NY Fed October economic calendar lists initial claims Oct 1 and Oct 8 at 8:30 AM ET and links to DOL. The DOL-linked data endpoint timed out during inspection; dates/times are verified on the date-specific NY Fed calendar, while the report-week detail is not yet listed.
  • EIA verified Natural Gas Storage for Oct 1 at 10:30 AM; its page did not yet identify the next Oct 8 release. Petroleum Status timing for this window was not date-specifically verifiable, so no oil-inventory event is shown. STEO is scheduled Oct 6, 12:00-12:15 PM ET.
  • TreasuryDirect confirms Oct 1 4- and 8-week bill bid cutoffs (11:00 AM noncompetitive; 11:30 AM competitive). Tentative Oct 6-8 bill/note auction dates lack announced exact bid-close times; omitted from timed rows pending official announcements.
  • BEA lists Services Supplied Through Affiliates (2024) on Oct 6 at 10:00 AM; omitted as an annual structural dataset with limited immediate ES/rates sensitivity. NY Fed also lists the Dallas Fed Weekly Economic Index (Oct 1 and 8, 11:30 AM), Economic Heterogeneity Indicators (Oct 2, 10:00 AM), and a Staff Nowcast (Oct 2, 12:45 PM); these routine model/weekly indicators are not treated as primary trade catalysts. Routine H.15 and commercial-paper tables are likewise omitted.
  • NAR lists no housing release through Oct 8 (next existing-home sales is Oct 13). NYSE calendar shows no U.S. cash-market holiday or shortened session during Oct 1-8; Sep 30 quarter-end has passed.
  • Market snapshot uses one delayed Yahoo Finance source; quotes are labeled by observation/session. No unavailable quote was substituted or inferred.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
Keep risk sized for today's 10:00 AM ISM and cluster of Fed speakers, with Friday payrolls the highest-impact near-term catalyst. Yields rose 3 bp and MOVE is moderate; require ES price confirmation before treating an overnight move as durable. Scenario framework, not a directional forecast.
INVALIDATION
Reassess a range or continuation thesis if ES breaks and holds outside the overnight range with confirming Treasury-yield/volatility repricing, or if payrolls materially shifts the expected policy path. Not a trade signal.
